question: Can the Acha Reef research lead be localized to Tagkawayan, Quezon, and does the accessible atlas copy contain site-specific fish data?
purpose: Cross-check source-described place identity and retrieve the historic atlas chapter. This is not a fish survey, current marine-protected-area verification, legal-boundary review, or geometry task.
searchMethod: Reviewed the official CALABARZON Regional Physical Framework Plan 2004-2030 Volume 2 at printed pages 47-48; checked the accessible DOST-NAST-hosted Atlas of Philippine Coral Reefs PDF, its title/copyright page and contents; and compared the Acha wording with the already-reviewed 2003 WWF Ragay Gulf report. The hosted atlas file was checked locally and contains 13 PDF pages. This is a bounded place and access review, not an exhaustive legal or biodiversity search.

findings.regionalPlan: The 2004-2030 regional plan names Acha Reef as a wetland located in Ragay Gulf, Tagkawayan, Quezon, reports an area of 500 hectares, and describes coral habitat for fish and other marine-animal groups. The plan gives no fish taxonomy, survey station, dates, technical boundary, or validated geometry in the reviewed section. Its condition and illegal-fishing descriptions are historical planning context only.
findings.atlasRetrieval: The contents of the 2002 Atlas of Philippine Coral Reefs list Ragay Gulf at p. 64, Acha Reef Fish Sanctuary at p. 69, and Alibijaban Fish Sanctuary at p. 71. The accessible NAST-hosted PDF copy is only 13 pages of front matter and contents; it does not include the cited chapters. The book states all rights reserved and permission required for reproduction. No chapter taxa or site results were extracted.
findings.wwfCrossCheck: The 2003 WWF-Philippines report names Acha Reef among Ragay Gulf sanctuary context and reports a gulf-level aggregate of 296 fish species in 18 families. It provides no species checklist, dates, stations, effort, or allocation of the aggregate to Acha Reef or Alibijaban.
findings.identityLimits: The repeated Acha Reef name and Ragay Gulf context support a distinct source-named reef research lead at Tagkawayan. The available evidence does not establish a current sanctuary designation, a legal boundary, reef polygon, or site-resolved fish record. The 500-hectare figure is a source-reported area statement, not geometry.

accessAndRights.regionalPlan: Official CALABARZON-hosted PDF reviewed; no item-specific open reuse license identified. Retain citation and short factual locality notes only.
accessAndRights.atlas: NAST/DOST-hosted partial copy identifies a 2002 PhilReefs publication, copyright 2002 PhilReefs, all rights reserved; reproduction requires publisher permission. Obtain authorized chapter access or use independent rights-cleared sources.
accessAndRights.rawRetention: No raw PDFs or copied source tables were added to the repository.

decision.reason: The official plan supports a source-described locality and reported area, while the atlas and WWF materials do not expose Acha-specific species records or current boundary/legal status.

nextAction: Seek an authorized copy of the Atlas chapter listed at p. 69 or an independent dated, station-resolved, rights-cleared fish survey for Acha Reef. In parallel, locate current official sanctuary designation and technical boundary records as a separate legal/geospatial source task; keep the reported 500 hectares out of map geometry.

sources.supports: Plan title and publication context; Acha Reef locality in Ragay Gulf, Tagkawayan, Quezon; source-reported 500-hectare area and historical habitat context.
Atlas title/copyright notice and contents listing Ragay Gulf, Acha Reef Fish Sanctuary and Alibijaban Fish Sanctuary chapters; the retrieved copy does not contain chapter text.
Historical Ragay Gulf fish-census aggregate and sanctuary context, without Acha-specific allocation.
